subject: Slot planning & KV-cache sensitivity — input for next week's QBR
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Slot planning & KV-cache sensitivity — input for next week's QBR
Attachments: qbr_slot_modeling_v2.xlsx (xlsx), kvcache-batching-sims.pdf (pdf)

Team —

As we finalize the QBR slides, we need a short, decision-focused slice on infra capacity and unit economics that the leadership panel can digest in one slide + one appendix table. High-level ask below — can each of you reply in-thread with the numbers/assumptions you own by EOD today so I can synthesize?

Primary questions (please answer inline):
- Baseline slot inventory and peak slot demand for the last 30d (p95 daily peak).
- Observed avg slot utilization (30d) and 95th percentile tail.
- Cost per slot-hour (effective after reserved pricing & infra overhead).
- Batching sensitivity: approximate throughput % uplift at median prompt length (we've been using 64 tokens median).
- KV-cache / prefix caching impact: % token reduction for typical chat workloads and observed cold-cache penalty windows.

Decision framing we need on the slide:
- Two scenarios: conservative (minimal caching, modest batching) vs optimistic (aggressive KV cache + larger batching).
- Show cost / 1M tokens under both scenarios and runway impact (months of free credits equivalent).

Deliverables and deadlines:
- Numbers (bullet answers to the questions above) by EOD 6/20 — I will pull and normalize.
- 1-slide appendix (single PDF) with assumptions + sensitivity ranges by 6/22 for the QBR pack.

I'm attaching the latest slot modeling workbook and the KV-cache sims I ran on last week's traces. If you think we need additional traces or a quick microbenchmark before 6/22, call it out here and I'll prioritize.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, Infrastructure Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Slot planning & KV-cache sensitivity — input for next week's QBR
Attachments: slot-run-rates.csv (csv)

Soojin — quick numbers from the infra-side; attaching the run-rate exports for the past 30d. I'll follow up with a short table for the slide but want to get these on record now.

Baseline / inventory:
- Provisioned GPU slots (steady state): 140 slots (mixed A100/V100-equivalent group).
- Observed p95 daily peak (30d): 126 slots.

Utilization:
- 30d average utilization (per-slot busy fraction): 0.61 (61%).
- 95th percentile (per-day peak hour utilization across slots): ~0.88.

Effective cost per slot-hour (blended after reserved commitments + infra overhead):
- Blended cost: $2.95 / slot-hour (this includes infra ops & network amortization).

Batching sensitivity (median prompt length ~64 tokens):
- Observed throughput uplift with continuous batching configured: +12% throughput at current queueing profile.
- With more aggressive batching (raise latency SLO to 250ms for tail), we see up to +22% throughput on microbenchmarks (but tail latencies increase ~35ms).

KV-cache / prefix caching impact (chat traces):
- On average, prefix caching reduces token generation by ~20% across our sampled chat workloads.
- Cold-cache penalty window: first 10–12 requests to a session see no benefit; for sessions longer than 3 turns, net token savings stabilize.

Notes / caveats:
- The sims I ran assume current model variants; quantization or switching to smaller model families changes the numbers materially.
- If we simulate a traffic burst scenario (50% above p95), queueing increases and effective batching uplift drops to ~6–8%.

Actionable: I'll drop a short CSV (attached) with the slot rates and a small assumptions table. If you want a worst-case runway calc (no KV-cache + no batching uplift) and a best-case calc (aggressive caching + 25% batching), say the word and I'll produce both by EOD.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Orchestration

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T12:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Slot planning & KV-cache sensitivity — input for next week's QBR

Thanks — this is a good start. A few quick requests so the leadership slide is actionable (I want the board to be able to read it in ~30s):

1) Please produce two scalar numbers we can show on the slide (and the assumptions in the appendix):
   - Cost / 1M generated tokens (conservative) — assume no KV-cache and minimal batching.
   - Cost / 1M generated tokens (optimistic) — assume KV-cache = 20% token reduction and batching uplift = 20%.

2) Include an expected tail-latency delta for optimistic vs conservative (we care about 95th token latency). If optimistic scenario increases 95th token latency by more than 25ms, flag it as a trade-off.

3) Prioritize the QBR narrative: we'd prefer to frame the optimistic case as an achievable operational lever (KV-cache + small batching config) rather than a risky latency trade-off. If the optimistic case materially degrades tail latency, mark it as "needs mitigation" and include the mitigation options (prefetch, partial KV warming, reserved hot slots).

Karthik — can you produce the two scalar cost numbers plus the 95th-latency delta by EOD? I can then shape the slide and add the impact to runway (months of runway preserved). If you want me to temp-assign someone in PME to make the appendix slide, I can.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick synthesis and next steps from me:

Synthesis (for the slide):
- Conservative scenario (presentation): assume current provisioned slots, no KV-cache benefit, batching uplift = +5% (safety). Cost / 1M tokens = $X (I'll let Karthik provide the scalar).
- Optimistic scenario: KV-cache = 20% token reduction (per Karthik), batching uplift = +20% (operational if we accept a modest tail increase). Show cost delta and months of runway preserved.

Immediate asks (actions):
1) Karthik: produce the two scalar cost / 1M tokens and the expected 95th-token latency delta for optimistic vs conservative by EOD. Put the assumptions in a single appendix slide.
2) Soojin: I'll need the normalized slot-hour blended cost in the same slide (what you're already tracking in the workbook).
3) Lauren: if you want a short framing bullet for the board (one sentence), send it by EOD 6/21 and I'll include.

I'll draft the two-slide QBR piece (summary + appendix) once I have Karthik's numbers. If we want to include finance-level cost amortization or reserve accounting in the QBR, flag it — I will not loop finance into the main slide unless the board asks, but we should be ready to provide a run-rate to finance in a breakout.

I'll also note a potential upside: if we can get even modest KV-cache adoption in the customer beta (see the workbook), the optimistic case becomes much more likely — call that out in the appendix.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Cloud Economics
Redwood Inference
